overall: Atlanta hit a running maximum of 91.4°F today, with the peak occurring around 16:19 ET, well above what most NWP models had forecast. A convective event (consistent with the NWS-forecast 70% PoP for tonight) caused a sharp temperature crash — from ~89-91°F at 16:52 down to 80.6°F by 17:52 — confirming storm passage. As of 23:00 ET, the temperature is 78.8°F and cooling steadily; the day's peak is definitively behind us.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models significantly underforecast today's high: ECMWF at 87.5°F and NBM at 86.8°F missed by roughly 4°F, while HRRR at 90.1°F came closest but still fell short of the 91.4°F observed max. The INTRADAY model (96.8% for 90-91°F bucket) correctly captured the outcome once real-time observations were incorporated, while the META model's elevated probability in the 92-95°F range suggests it had not yet fully absorbed the give-up classifier signal that fired at hour 14.67.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F — it is 23:00 ET, the current temperature is 78.8°F and falling, and the running max has been flat at 91.4°F since 17:00. There is essentially zero probability of a new daily high being set overnight. Confidence is extremely high (>99%) that the final recorded TMAX will be 91.4°F.
